messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up idea — propose an 'attr slots' primitive on spans/metrics to unify cost attribution across tracing and metrics. Want quick sanity check before I write a full RFC.

maria: Can you sketch what an 'attr slot' looks like? Is this just another label or a structured header?

alex: Short sketch: attr slot = small fixed-length slot that references a low-cardinality key + optional late-bound value. Two forms: inline header for edge services, and envelope for internal services. Example header:```X-Attr-Slots: billing=payments;env=prod;cost_key=tenant_123```or JSON envelope:```{"attr_slots":["billing:payments","env:prod","cost_key:tenant_123"]}```

lee: main concern = cardinality. If services start stuffing user IDs into slots we'll blow up metrics/ingest. How do we prevent that?

alex: Agree. Proposal: slot schema enforces type + cardinality class. E.g. slot#1=anchor (low-cardinality), slot#2=freeform (only used in late-enrich, not indexed). Ingest rules: anchor slots get indexed for queries/billing, freeform slots stored in blob for debug only.

jonathan: Sounds ok. Also think we should map existing billing_key flow to slot#1 so current cost attribution pipelines don't need immediate changes. Migration path: populates slot#1 from billing_key until rollout complete.

maria: How about the gateway boundary? Do we require edge proxies to set header, or let SDKs populate envelope?

alex: Option A: edge proxies set header (fast path, small overhead). Option B: SDKs write envelope (richer, but needs SDK upgrade). Plan: accept both. Edge header takes precedence; SDK envelope can add extra non-indexed slots.

lee: Rollout ops: need flaggable ingestion filter so we can opt-in services and roll back if cardinality spikes. Also add hard limits per tenant + telemetry alerts.

alex: Yep — part of RFC: compat rules, ingress throttles, slot quotas per tenant, and auto-rewrite to 'unknown' when slot cardinality > N/day. We'll also include a migration checklist.

jonathan: Sampling implications — if we drop spans early, we lose slot data. We should prefer lightweight header so sampling happens after header read.

alex: Good catch. Order of ops: read headers at gateway prior to sampling decision; record anchor slots into sampling metadata. Late-enrich can add high-card data but won't affect core billing tags.

maria: Any changes to query surface? Will users query by slot name?

alex: We'll expose a small set of indexed slot fields (anchor slots) in the query API. Non-indexed slots only available via raw span payloads. Query engine change: map slot->column and keep fallback to blob lookup for ad-hoc.

lee: Perf tests? I can queue a lightweight ingest perf run with synthetic anchors + a few freeform fields to validate index growth.

sre-bot: perf-test-runner: scheduled perf job 4412224000 for 'attr-slots-sim' (expected ~2h). Results will be posted in #eng-platform.

alex: Thanks — I'll draft RFC with options (header vs envelope), slot schema, ingest controls, and rollout plan. Will include a small compatibility shim to copy billing_key->slot#1. Tagging @eng-platform for review. :+1:
